extracted.intended_audience: pipeline operators, pipeline safety compliance officers, and PHMSA/regulatory staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for installation, operation, monitoring, maintenance, notification, and post-incident analysis of rupture-mitigation valves (RMVs) and alternative equivalent technologies on onshore gas transmission, gathering, and hazardous liquid/CO2 pipelines, including timing, spacing, testing, and reporting obligations to PHMSA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design/installation of Type C gathering lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (h) for pipe and components made with composite materials, the design, installation, construction, initial inspection, and initial testing of a new, replaced, relocated, or otherwise changed Type C gathering line, must be done in accordance with the requirements in subparts B though G and J of this part applicable to transmission lines. Compliance with §§192.67, 192.127, 192.179(e), 192.179(f), 192.205, 192.227(c), 192.285(e), 192.506, 192.634, and 192.636 is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies Type-transmission-line requirements to Type C gathering lines except where specifically exempted; consult listed sections for applicability and explicit exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 90-day PHMSA notification for alternative methods
rubrics_metrics.description: If an operator submits, pursuant to listed sections, a notification for use of a different integrity assessment method, analytical method, sampling approach, or technique (e.g., 'other technology' or 'alternative equivalent technology') than otherwise prescribed, that notification must be submitted to PHMSA for review at least 90 days in advance of using the other method, approach, compliance timeline, or technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator may proceed to use the other method 91 days after submitting the notification unless PHMSA objects or requests more time/information; applies across many specific sections cited (e.g., §192.8, §192.179, §195.258, §195.418, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: RMV installation for new onshore transmission ≥6 inches
rubrics_metrics.description: For onshore transmission pipeline segments with diameters ≥6 inches constructed after April 10, 2023, the operator must install rupture-mitigation valves (RMV) or an alternative equivalent technology whenever a valve must be installed to meet the appropriate valve spacing requirements of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative equivalent technology requires PHMSA notification; all RMVs and alternatives installed pursuant must meet requirements of §§192.634 and 192.636; exempted for pipeline segments in Class 1 or Class 2 locations with PIR ≤150 feet; operator may request compliance-deadline extension if economically/technically/operationally infeasible by demonstrating to PHMSA per §192.18.

rubrics_metrics.name: RMV installation for entirely replaced segments (gas)
rubrics_metrics.description: For entirely replaced onshore transmission pipeline segments (as defined), with diameters ≥6 inches and installed after April 10, 2023, the operator must install RMVs or an alternative equivalent technology whenever a valve must be installed to meet appropriate valve spacing requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies when replacement project involves a valve (addition/replacement/removal); exemptions for Class 1 or Class 2 with PIR ≤150 feet; alternative equivalent technology requires PHMSA notification per §192.18; extension process same as for new segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification content and manual-valve demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: If an operator elects to use alternative equivalent technology, the operator must notify PHMSA and include a technical and safety evaluation in its notice. An operator requesting use of manual valves as an alternative equivalent technology must include a demonstration that installation of an RMV as otherwise required would be economically, technically, or operationally infeasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valves installed as alternative equivalent technology must comply with §§192.634 and 192.636; a manual compressor station valve at a continuously manned station may be used as an alternative without §192.18 notification but must comply with §192.636.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve spacing exemption for pipe replacements (§192.179(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: The valve spacing requirements of paragraph (a) do not apply to pipe replacements on a pipeline if the distance between each point on the pipeline and the nearest valve does not exceed specified maximums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximums: (1) 4 miles in Class 4 locations (total spacing ≤8 miles); (2) 7.5 miles in Class 3 locations (total spacing ≤15 miles); (3) 10 miles in Class 1 or 2 locations (total spacing ≤20 miles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Class location change triggers valve requirements (§192.610(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a class location change occurs after October 5, 2022 and results in pipe replacement of 2 or more miles in the aggregate within any 5 contiguous miles within a 24-month period to meet MAOP requirements, then §§192.179, 192.634, and 192.636 apply to the new class location and the operator must install valves (including RMVs or alternatives) as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such valves must be installed within 24 months of the class location change in accordance with timing in §192.611(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve obligations for smaller class-location replacements (§192.610(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a class location change after Oct 5, 2022 results in pipe replacement of less than 2 miles within 5 contiguous miles during a 24‑month period to meet MAOP, then within 24 months operator must either (1) comply with valve spacing requirements of §192.179(a) for the replaced segment; or (2) install or use existing RMVs/alternatives so the replaced segments are between at least two RMVs and distance between RMVs for replaced segment must not exceed 20 miles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (b) does not apply to replacements <1,000 feet within any one contiguous mile during any 24‑month period; RMVs/alternatives must comply with applicable §192.636 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency plan: communications and liaison (§192.615(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must establish and maintain adequate means of communication with the appropriate public safety answering point (9‑1‑1 emergency call center), where direct access is available, and fire, police, and other public officials. Operators may establish liaison with local emergency coordinating agencies in lieu of communicating individually with each entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator must determine responsibilities, resources, jurisdictional areas, and emergency contact telephone numbers for local and out-of-area responders and inform such officials about the operator's ability to respond and means of communication during emergencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency plan: necessary mitigative actions (§192.615(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators must take necessary actions, including but not limited to emergency shutdown, valve shut-off, or pressure reduction, in any section of the operator's pipeline system to minimize hazards of released gas to life, property, or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mandatory elements of emergency response plans and must be actionable by operations personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate notification to PSAP on potential rupture (§192.615(a)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: The operator must immediately and directly notify the appropriate public safety answering point or other coordinating agency for communities/jurisdictions in which the pipeline is located after receiving a notification of potential rupture, to coordinate and share information to determine the location of any release, regardless of whether the segment is subject to §§192.179, 192.634, or 192.636.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to planned and actual responses during an emergency; ensures prompt coordination with local emergency services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller actions during emergency (§192.615(a)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency plans must specify actions required to be taken by a controller during an emergency in accordance with the operator's emergency plans and requirements set forth in §§192.631, 192.634, and 192.636.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controllers must be trained and procedures must be aligned with specific valve and mitigation requirements in cited sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written rupture identification procedures (§192.615(a)(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each operator must develop written rupture identification procedures to evaluate and identify whether a notification of potential rupture is an actual rupture event or a non-rupture event. Procedures must at minimum specify sources of information, operational factors, and other criteria used by personnel to evaluate notifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For operators installing valves per §192.179(e)/(f) or subject to §192.634, procedures must provide for rupture identification as soon as practicable. Documentation should include who evaluates, what indicators are used, and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-failure investigation procedures (§192.617(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each operator must establish and follow procedures for investigating and analyzing failures and incidents, including sending failed pipe, component, or equipment for laboratory testing or examination where appropriate, to determine causes/contributing factors and minimize recurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures must support root-cause analysis and evidence preservation for future risk-reduction actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of lessons learned (§192.617(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each operator must develop, implement, and incorporate lessons learned from post-failure or incident reviews into its written procedures, including personnel training and qualification programs, and design, construction, testing, maintenance, operations, and emergency procedure manuals and specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an ongoing systems-improvement requirement; updates to manuals and training must be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-incident analysis when RMV closure involved (§192.617(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an incident on an onshore gas transmission pipeline or Type A gathering pipeline involves closure of an RMV or alternative equivalent technology, the operator must conduct a post-incident analysis of all factors that may have impacted release volume and consequences and identify/implement O&M measures to prevent or minimize future consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis must include detection, identification, operational response, system shutdown, effectiveness of procedures and systems (SCADA, communications, valve shut-off, personnel), actual response time from rupture identification to mitigative actions, location/timeliness of RMV actuation, and other operator-deemed relevant factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rupture post-failure summary and records (§192.617(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a failure/incident involves identification of a rupture or closure of an RMV/alternative, operator must complete a summary of the post-failure review within 90 days, conduct quarterly status reviews while investigation pending, and have final summary and associated documents reviewed, dated, and signed by an appropriate senior executive officer. Final summary and all documents/lessons learned must be kept for the useful life of the pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly status reviews required until final; records retention is long-term (useful life) and requires senior executive certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and timing for RMVs on onshore transmission in HCAs/Class 3/4 (§192.634(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: For new or entirely replaced onshore transmission pipeline segments ≥6 inches located in HCAs or Class 3 or Class 4 locations and installed after April 10, 2023, operator must install or use existing RMVs or alternative equivalent technology according to this section and §§192.179 and 192.636. RMVs and alternatives must be operational within 14 days of placing new or replaced segment into service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator may request extension of 14-day operation requirement if demonstration shows infeasibility under §192.18; requirement applies to all applicable pipe replacement projects even if project does not add/replace a valve; does not apply to Class 1/Class 2 segments with PIR ≤150 feet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and requirements of a 'shut-off segment' (§192.634(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'shut-off segment' means the pipe located between the upstream valve closest to the upstream endpoint of the new/replaced HCA/Class3/Class4 segment and the downstream valve closest to the downstream endpoint so that the entirety of the segment within the HCA/Class location is between at least two RMVs or alternatives. If crossovers/laterals connect to the shut-off segment between valves, the shut-off segment must extend to a valve on those connections so that, when all valves are closed, there is no flow path to the rupture site (except residual gas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator not required to select the closest valve as the RMV; manual compressor station valve at a continuously manned station may be used as alternative if able to be closed within 30 minutes following rupture identification; such manual compressor station valve used as alternative does not require §192.18 notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum valve spacing for shut-off segments (§192.634(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A pipeline subject to paragraph (a) must have RMVs or alternative equivalent technology on upstream and downstream sides of the pipeline segment. The distance between RMVs/alternatives must not exceed: (i) 8 miles for any Class 4 location; (ii) 15 miles for any Class 3 location; or (iii) 20 miles for all other locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are absolute maximum distances for RMV placement on shut-off segments; multiple Class 3/4 or HCA segments may be in a single shut-off segment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laterals and check-valve alternative rules (§192.634(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Laterals contributing <5% of total shut-off segment volume may have RMVs/alternatives meeting actuation requirements located elsewhere, provided cumulative laterals do not exceed 5% of total shut-off volume. For laterals ≤12 inches diameter, a check valve that prevents flow into the shut-off segment may be used as an alternative equivalent technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check valves used as alternative are not subject to §192.636 but must be inspected, operated, and remediated per §192.745 (including for closure and leakage); operator must notify PHMSA per §§192.18 and 192.179 and develop/implement maintenance procedures meeting §192.745.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crossovers: locked manual valves as alternative (§192.634(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: An operator may use a manual valve as an alternative equivalent technology for a crossover connection if, during normal operations, the valve is closed to prevent flow by use of a locking device or other means designed to prevent opening by unauthorized persons. The operator must develop and implement operating procedures and document the valve has been closed and locked per the operator's lock-out/tag-out procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator using such manual valve as alternative must notify PHMSA in accordance with §§192.18 and 192.179.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual valve operation time accounting (§192.634(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators using a manual valve as an alternative must develop and implement operating procedures designating and locating nearby personnel to ensure valve shut-off in accordance with this section and §192.636. Manual operation timing must include assembly of personnel, acquisition of tools/equipment, driving time under heavy traffic at posted speed limit, walking time to access valve, and time to shut off all valves manually, not to exceed maximum response time under §192.636(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures must be realistic and account for worst-case travel and mobilization times to meet response-time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'notification of potential rupture' (§192.635)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'notification of potential rupture' refers to the notification to or observation by an operator of one or more indicia of a potential unintentional/uncontrolled large-volume gas release: (1) unanticipated/unexplained pressure loss outside normal operating pressures — pressure loss >10% within 15 minutes unless operator documents a different threshold due to flow dynamics; (2) unanticipated/unexplained flow rate change, pressure change, equipment function, or other pipeline instrumentation indication that may represent paragraph (a)(1); (3) any unanticipated/unexplained rapid release of a large volume of gas, a fire, or explosion in immediate vicinity of pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notification of potential rupture occurs when the operator first receives notice of or observes one of these events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rupture identification and valve shut-off time requirement (§192.636(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An operator must, as soon as practicable but within 30 minutes of rupture identification (see §192.615(a)(12)), fully close any RMVs or alternative equivalent technologies necessary to minimize volume of gas released and mitigate consequences of a rupture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 30-minute closure requirement is a firm maximum for required valve action unless an exception applies under §192.636(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception to 30-minute closure (leave valve open) (§192.636(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: An operator may leave an RMV or alternative open for >30 minutes if the operator has previously established in operating procedures and demonstrated within a notice under §192.18 for PHMSA review that closing the valve would be detrimental to public safety. The request must be coordinated with appropriate local emergency responders, and operator and responders must determine it is safe to leave valve open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must have written procedures for deciding whether to leave valve open, including plans to communicate with responders and minimize environmental impacts; these must be submitted as part of PHMSA notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valve monitoring and operation capabilities (§192.636(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An RMV or alternative must be capable of being monitored or controlled remotely or by on-site personnel: (1) Operated during normal, abnormal, and emergency operating conditions; (2) Monitored for valve status (open/closed/partial), upstream pressure, and downstream pressure; (3) Have a back-up power source to maintain SCADA or other remote communications for RCV/ASV operational status, or be monitored/controlled by on-site personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ASVs, operator does not need remote status monitoring if capability exists to monitor pressures or gas flow rate within each pipeline segment between RMVs to identify and locate a rupture; segments with manual valves must have capability to monitor pressures/flow to identify/locate ruptures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring of valve shut-off response status (§192.636(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The position and operational status of an RMV must be appropriately monitored through electronic communication with remote instrumentation or other equivalent means. An operator does not need to monitor remotely an ASV's status if the operator can monitor pressures or flow to identify and locate a rupture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic monitoring must reliably indicate valve position and operational health for timely response and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flow modeling requirement for ASV use as RMV (§192.636(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to using an ASV as an RMV, an operator must conduct flow modeling for the shut-off segment and any laterals feeding it, so the valve will close within 30 minutes or less following rupture identification. The modeling must include anticipated maximum, normal, and other flow volumes/pressures/conditions anticipated during the year (not exceeding 15 months), and model flow between RMVs/alternatives and any looped pipelines or receipt tie-ins. Include a time/pressure chart for the segment containing the ASV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If operating conditions change that could affect ASV set pressures and 30-minute closure time, operator must conduct new flow model and reset ASV pressures prior to next review per §192.745; conduct modeling before making flow condition changes that could render 30-minute closure unachievable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual valves exemption request in non-HCA Class 1 (§192.636(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: For pipeline segments in a Class 1 location that do not meet HCA definition, an operator submitting a notification for use of manual valves as an alternative may also request an exemption from §192.636(b) (the 30-minute closure requirement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exemption must be requested in the same notification submitted pursuant to §§192.18 and 192.179.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCV point-to-point SCADA verification (§192.745(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each remote-control valve (RCV) installed under §192.179 or §192.634, an operator must conduct a point-to-point verification between SCADA system displays and the installed valves, sensors, and communications equipment, in accordance with §192.631(c) and (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification ensures SCADA indications correspond to physical valve/sensor states and communications are reliable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual/randomized 30-minute response validation drills for manual alternatives (§192.745(d)(1)-(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each manually or locally operated alternative equivalent technology, operators must achieve a valve closure time of 30 minutes or less through an initial drill and periodic validation. Within each pipeline system and each operating/maintenance field work unit, operators must randomly select a valve serving as an alternative in lieu of an RMV for an annual 30-minute-total response time validation drill simulating worst-case conditions. Operators are not required to fully close the valve during the drill; minimum 25% closure is sufficient to demonstrate compliance unless more is operationally required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Response drill must occur at least once each calendar year with intervals not exceeding 15 months. Operators must document review and results for each drill phase including confirming rupture and shut-off time, and include their random-selection method in written procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failed drill corrective actions and lessons learned (§192.745(d)(3)-(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the 30‑minute maximum response time cannot be achieved during the drill, the operator must revise response efforts to achieve compliance as soon as practicable but no later than 12 months after the drill. Alternative valve shut-off measures must be in place within 7 days of a failed drill. Based on drill results, operator must include lessons learned in training/qualifications, manuals, and other identified areas needing improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failed-drill interim measures and documented improvements are mandatory; timelines (7 days interim, 12 months full compliance) are specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption from drill requirements for manually exempted valves (§192.745(d)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (d) drill requirements do not apply to manual valves that have been exempted from §192.636(b) pursuant to §192.636(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators must track which valves hold exemptions to avoid unnecessary drill obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial measures for inoperable valves (§192.745(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each operator must develop and implement remedial measures to correct any valve installed under §192.179(e)/(f) or §192.634 that is indicated to be inoperable or unable to maintain effective shut-off: (1) Repair or replace as soon as practicable but no later than 12 months after finding; (2) Designate an alternative valve acting as an RMV within 7 calendar days while repairs are made and document an interim response plan to maintain safety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operator may request extension from PHMSA per §192.18 if repair/replacement within 12 months is infeasible; designated interim valves are not required to comply with valve spacing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASV shut-in pressure documentation and periodic confirmation (§192.745(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An operator using an ASV as an RMV must document and confirm the ASV shut-in pressures on a calendar year basis not to exceed 15 months. ASV shut-in set pressures must be proven and reset individually at each ASV as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic confirmation must align with flow-modeling assumptions and reflect any operational changes; documentation required for compliance records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk analysis requirement to install RMV or equivalent (§192.935(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an operator determines, based on a risk analysis, that an RMV or alternative equivalent technology would be an efficient means of adding protection to an HCA in the event of a gas release, the operator must install the RMV or alternative equivalent technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In making the determination, operator must at least evaluate: timing of leak detection and pipe shutdown capabilities, type of gas, operating pressure, rate of potential release, pipeline profile, potential for ignition, and location of nearest response personnel. RMV/equivalent installed must meet all other applicable requirements in the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic review and certification of risk analyses (§192.935(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk analyses and assessments conducted under paragraph (c) must be reviewed by the operator and certified by a senior executive of the company for operational matters that could affect rupture-mitigation processes/procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review/certification must occur once per calendar year with period between reviews not exceeding 15 months, and must also occur within 3 months of an incident or safety-related condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions added for Part 195 (entirely replaced, notification, RMV)
rubrics_metrics.description: §195.2 adds definitions: 'Entirely replaced onshore hazardous liquid or carbon dioxide pipeline segments' means where 2 or more miles of pipe, in the aggregate, have been replaced within any 5 contiguous miles within any 24-month period. 'Notification of Potential Rupture' means the notification to or observation by an operator of indicia identified in §195.417. 'Rupture-mitigation valve' means an ASV or RCV that an operator uses to minimize the volume of hazardous liquid or CO2 released and mitigate rupture consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions align terminology in Part 195 with Part 192 requirements and set thresholds for replacement and notification applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to notify PHMSA for Part 195 (§195.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: An operator must provide any notification required by Part 195 by: (1) sending notification by email to InformationResourcesManager@dot.gov; or (2) mailing to ATTN: Information Resources Manager, DOT/PHMSA/OPS, East Building, 2nd Floor, E22-321, 1200 New Jersey Ave. SE, Washington, DC 20590. Operator must also notify appropriate State/local pipeline safety authority when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise specified, notification requesting use of different methods/alternate technologies must be submitted at least 90 days in advance; operator may proceed after 91 days unless PHMSA objects or requires additional time/information.

rubrics_metrics.name: RMV and alternative requirements for onshore hazardous liquid/CO2 pipelines (§195.258(c)-(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For all onshore hazardous liquid or CO2 pipeline segments with diameters ≥6 inches constructed after April 10, 2023, operator must install RMVs or an alternative equivalent technology whenever a valve must be installed to meet valve spacing requirements. For entirely replaced onshore segments replaced after April 10, 2023, operator must install RMVs or alternatives whenever a valve must be installed to meet spacing. An operator electing to use alternative equivalent technology must notify PHMSA and include a technical and safety evaluation in its notice; valves installed as alternatives must comply with §§195.418, 195.419, and 195.420.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators may request extension of installation deadlines if economically/technically/operationally infeasible via §195.18 notification procedures; valves installed must meet cross-referenced Part 195 requirements.
